What interests you about this role, and how do your skills or experience make you a good fit?
checks.expected: What draws me to Laminar is that the models are judged in contact with messy physical processes, not just clean benchmarks. That matches the work I have enjoyed most: building experiments that reveal when models generalize, fail, or pick up confounds. At Arborphy AI, I designed dual-encoder plant-identification models, compared encoder and fusion choices, and ran individual-disjoint, multi-seed, and held-out evaluations. At Columbia Zuckerman, I worked on self-supervised denoising for calcium-imaging data with ablations across architectures, losses, and training settings. I also built real-time robotics vision pipelines with optimized inference. Laminar’s focus on preprocessing, feature extraction, drift/anomaly robustness, and clean ML tooling is a strong match for my Python, PyTorch, and scikit-learn background and my habit of turning research questions into reproducible code.
